newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Howard launches push for Australian tax reform.
newsitem.headline: Howard launches push for Australian tax reform.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard launched a campaign for tax reform on Thursday, saying the current system put too great a burden on income and discouraged saving.
"The last great outpost of economic backwardness in the Australian economy ... is the taxation system," Howard told a mining industry dinner.
"We should set about constructing a more effective taxation system for the new millennium."
Taxation reform, especially any proposal for a value-added tax (VAT) on consumption, has been an intensely controversial issue in Australia.

Howard's predecessor as Liberal-National leader, John Hewson, lost a seemingly unloseable election in 1993 after saying he would reform the tax system by cutting income tax and replacing the complex and inconsistent system of sales taxes with a comprehensive 15-percent VAT.

The then Labor government presided over near-record unemployment in 1993 but the electorate rejected Hewson and his goods and services tax. Howard explictly promised not to introduce one before winning the 1996 election.
But the business community has continued to campaign for a broad-based consumption tax and two opinion polls published this week showed majority support for such a measure.
In his Thursday speech Howard said the current system relied too much on income tax. Australia's top marginal rate is near 50 percent.
Current taxes penalised export industries and savings, he said, adding: "We also have a taxation system that is too easily avoided in a number of areas."

Howard and Treasurer Peter Costello have made a few tentative statements in recent weeks endorsing the notion of a goods and services tax, but both have been quick to restate the commitment not to introduce one in their current term of office, which will expire in early 1999.
Howard's statement that the country should set about fixing the tax system for the new millennium is his strongest statement on the subject so far.
